newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Gold vulnerable at 12-year lows.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Gold vulnerable at 12-year lows.

text.p: SPOT NY CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI14 * MA10 * MA30
Gold prices slumped to 12-year lows on Australian central bank gold sales and remain vulnerable to further losses, dealers and analysts said on Friday.
But near-term prices may consolidate as gold is oversold, physical demand is picking up and U.S. markets are closed.

GOLD - Gold prices fell sharply in late New York trading on Thursday, easily slicing through critical support at $325.10 per ounce, a level last touched in 1993 and the lowest point gold had reached since the mid-1980s.
Values continued declining in Asian trading and early European business and gold was last indicated at $322.80/$323.30.

"The negative effect for gold was news that the Reserve Bank of Australia had 167 tonnes of gold, which was a confirmation that central banks are really tempted to sell gold reserves," said analyst Hanspeter Hausherr of Zurich-based Swiss Bank Corporation.
"Now the market is futher convinced this will go on so the prices will go still lower."
Analysts said prices could take a breather at current levels in the very near term, with technical indicators such as the 14-day Relative Strength Index showing the market was heavily oversold.
"We could see some consolidation in the area of $323-$325 today," Hausherr said, adding that some interim support may also been seen in the $318-$320 level.
Physical offtake was likely to pick up at these sharply lower levels, and in the absence of the U.S. market, due to the Independence Day holiday, business will be thinner than usual.
But in the longer term sharply lower values could be seen.
Commodity brokers GNI said in a commentary that a break below $325.10 "would signal a major long term top in the market and give a target of $280 in the short term."
